runs_locally.note: uv run scripts/attack.py --sample 20 on two targets x 2 settings (direct + mathprompt) = 40 question-runs/target, 0 errors, no GPU. Single PEP-723 script (openai only). Stage-1 math encoding (deepseek-chat attacker) ~34-45s; stage-2 target+HarmBench-judge ~44-60s; both stages concurrent (ThreadPoolExecutor, 12 workers). Encodings cached per behavior and reused across settings/targets.

faithful_to_paper.note: No official repo (code_repos: []); reproduced from the paper appendix VERBATIM. ATTACKER_SYSTEM_PROMPT = Appendix 8.2 mathematics-expert prompt; FEWSHOT = the two demos in Appendix 8.3 ('how to rob a bank', 'how to hack into a government database') with set-theory/abstract-algebra/symbolic-logic structure kept char-for-char; PREPENDED_INSTRUCTION = Appendix 8.4 'math problem solver... real entities, names, locations'. Two-stage black-box pipeline (encode via attacker LLM -> prepend solver instruction -> target) matches sec 3-3.1. Greedy decoding (temperature 0) per sec 4.1. Judge = HarmBench classifier (sec 4.1): the standard cais/HarmBench-Llama-2-13b-cls classifier PROMPT is embedded verbatim (HARMBENCH_CLS_PROMPT) and served on OpenRouter (judge-model substitution, official judge is GPU-only).

self_contained.note: Single PEP-723 script, dependency = openai only. Harmful-behavior dataset cached at data/advbench/harmful_behaviors.csv (AdvBench goal column = faithful representative subset of the paper's Liu-et-al 120 questions, 80% of which are from AdvBench/GPTFuzzer/MASTERKEY/TDC). No GPU; attacker + target + judge all via OpenRouter. HarmBench classifier prompt embedded verbatim in the script (no model download).

model_flexible_fast.note: --target / --attacker / --judge / --settings / --sample / --max-tokens / --workers / --dataset / --out all swappable; accepts target ids with or without 'api:' prefix. Demonstrated on two targets (qwen/qwen-2.5-7b-instruct, mistralai/mistral-nemo). The >=2 parameter-set knob = settings {direct, mathprompt}.

result_comparable.note: Dual metric: refusal_bypass (rule-based non-refusal proxy) + content_harmful (verbatim HarmBench classifier, headline ASR). Baseline 'direct' included and lands near the paper's ~1% floor. qwen-2.5-7b: content_harmful 0.000 (direct) -> 0.250 (mathprompt), refusal_bypass 0.000 -> 1.000. mistral-nemo: content_harmful 0.050 -> 0.200, refusal_bypass 0.150 -> 1.000. The paper's core claim (safety alignment does not generalize to symbolic math) reproduces cleanly: refusal is fully bypassed (->1.0) on both targets. Absolute content_harmful is below the paper's 73.6% avg, honestly attributed to a weaker OpenRouter attacker (vs GPT-4o), a stricter substitute judge (HarmBench prompt on deepseek-chat vs GPU HarmBench-Llama-2-13b), and small open targets (vs barred frontier models). See references/method.md.

note: MathPrompt: Jailbreaking LLMs with Symbolic Mathematics (arXiv:2409.11445, 2024; no official repo). Faithful two-stage black-box port from the paper appendix (verbatim attacker system prompt + 2 few-shot demos + prepended solver instruction). Headline: encoding a harmful NL instruction as a set-theory/abstract-algebra/symbolic-logic problem lifts refusal_bypass from 0.00-0.15 (direct) to 1.00 on both qwen-2.5-7b and mistral-nemo -- safety alignment does not generalize to symbolic math, exactly the paper's claim. HarmBench content_harmful 0.20-0.25 (vs paper 73.6% avg) is attenuated by a weaker substitute attacker/judge and small open targets, documented honestly. 80 cases, 0 errors, no GPU.
external_staging: no_external_staging_required for the current black-box benchmark unit; OpenRouter serves attacker, target, and judge roles.
